opening.text: Some puzzles have one piece that looks small. But the picture is not complete without it.
The Book of Mormon is a piece like that. It fits with the Bible, and the picture of Jesus Christ is fuller with both. Today I want to talk about this book.

mainMessage.text: The Book of Mormon is another testament of Jesus Christ. It joins the Bible. We can know it is true by asking God. It was written for our day. It gives us a safe foundation, and it gives us something good to share.

blocks.text: A piece that fits.
Nephi said they talk of Christ, rejoice in Christ, and write of Christ. At the end of his record, he urged everyone to believe in Christ and said these words teach us to do good.

And we talk of Christ, we rejoice in Christ, we preach of Christ, we prophesy of Christ, and we write according to our prophecies, that our children may know to what source they may look for a remission of their sins.

And now, my beloved brethren, and also Jew, and all ye ends of the earth, hearken unto these words and believe in Christ; and if ye believe not in these words believe in Christ. And if ye shall believe in Christ ye will believe in these words, for they are the words of Christ, and he hath given them unto me; and they teach all men that they should do good.

President Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this about the Book of Mormon in his talk “The Book of Mormon: What Would Your Life Be Like without It?” from the October 2017 general conference.
It is another testament of Jesus Christ.
Its whole purpose is to point to Him.
Two records, one purpose.
Ezekiel wrote about two sticks, one for Judah and one for Joseph, joined into one. Joseph of old was told that the writings of both peoples would grow together.

Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.

Wherefore, the fruit of thy loins shall write; and the fruit of the loins of Judah shall write; and that which shall be written by the fruit of thy loins, and also that which shall be written by the fruit of the loins of Judah, shall grow together, unto the confounding of false doctrines and laying down of contentions, and establishing peace among the fruit of thy loins, and bringing them to the knowledge of their fathers in the latter days, and also to the knowledge of my covenants, saith the Lord.
The Prophet Joseph Smith said this, as quoted in the Introduction to the Book of Mormon. It is a prophet’s statement, not a conference talk.

I told the brethren that the Book of Mormon was the most correct of any book on earth, and the keystone of our religion, and a man would get nearer to God by abiding by its precepts, than by any other book.
The Bible and the Book of Mormon stand side by side.
You can know it is true.
Moroni invited us to ask God with a sincere heart. The Savior said that if we choose to do God’s will, we will know.

And when ye shall receive these things, I would exhort you that ye would ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if these things are not true; and if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost. And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
President Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Book of Mormon: What Would Your Life Be Like without It?” from the October 2017 general conference.
I testify that the Book of Mormon is truly the word of God.
The invitation is open to everyone.
Made to fit our day.
Mormon said he saw our time and spoke to us as if we were present. Moroni said we will one day remember his words before God.

Behold, the Lord hath shown unto me great and marvelous things concerning that which must shortly come, at that day when these things shall come forth among you. Behold, I speak unto you as if ye were present, and yet ye are not. But behold, Jesus Christ hath shown you unto me, and I know your doing.

And I exhort you to remember these things; for the time speedily cometh that ye shall know that I lie not, for ye shall see me at the bar of God; and the Lord God will say unto you: Did I not declare my words unto you, which were written by this man, like as one crying from the dead, yea, even as one speaking out of the dust?
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in his article “The Book of Mormon Is the Word of God” in the January 1988 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

The Book of Mormon was written for us today. God is the author of the book. It is a record of a fallen people, compiled by inspired men for our blessing. Those people never had the book—it was meant for us. Mormon, the ancient prophet after whom the book is named, abridged centuries of records. God, who knows the end from the beginning, told him what to include in his abridgment that we would need for our day.
The book speaks to our questions today.
A safe foundation.
Helaman told his sons to build on Christ, the rock. Nephi said to press forward and feast on the word of Christ.

And now, my sons, remember, remember that it is upon the rock of our Redeemer, who is Christ, the Son of God, that ye must build your foundation; that when the devil shall send forth his mighty winds, yea, his shafts in the whirlwind, yea, when all his hail and his mighty storm shall beat upon you, it shall have no power over you to drag you down to the gulf of misery and endless wo, because of the rock upon which ye are built, which is a sure foundation, a foundation whereon if men build they cannot fall.

Wherefore, ye must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ, having a perfect brightness of hope, and a love of God and of all men. Wherefore, if ye shall press forward, feasting upon the word of Christ, and endure to the end, behold, thus saith the Father: Ye shall have eternal life.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Safety for the Soul” from the October 2009 general conference.
God always provides safety for the soul, and with the Book of Mormon, He has again done that in our time.
We do not have to face the storms alone.
Share the fruit.
Lehi found joy in the fruit and wanted his family to have it too. Alma wanted to bring souls to God.

And it came to pass that I beheld a tree, whose fruit was desirable to make one happy. And it came to pass that I did go forth and partake of the fruit thereof; and I beheld that it was most sweet, above all that I ever before tasted. Yea, and I beheld that the fruit thereof was white, to exceed all the whiteness that I had ever seen. And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit.

I know that which the Lord hath commanded me, and I glory in it. I do not glory of myself, but I glory in that which the Lord hath commanded me; yea, and this is my glory, that perhaps I may be an instrument in the hands of God to bring some soul to repentance; and this is my joy.
President Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Book of Mormon: What Would Your Life Be Like without It?” from the October 2017 general conference.
It contains the answers to life’s most compelling questions.
When something helps us, we want others to have it.

story.title: Nephi finds a way

blocks.text: Nephi was asked to get the brass plates, and it looked impossible. He answered his father.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
The plates were hard to get. But they held the words the family needed. In the same way, the Book of Mormon can fill the empty places in our lives.

story.title: By small and simple things

blocks.text: Alma gave his son Helaman the sacred records and told him how to guard them.

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
A book kept for hundreds of years may look like a small thing. But God uses small and simple means to bless many lives. The Book of Mormon is one of them.

story.title: Try the seed

blocks.text: Alma taught a crowd how to test the word of God, using a seed.

Now, we will compare the word unto a seed. Now, if ye give place, that a seed may be planted in your heart, behold, if it be a true seed, or a good seed, if ye do not cast it out by your unbelief, that ye will resist the Spirit of the Lord, behold, it will begin to swell within your breasts; and when you feel these swelling motions, ye will begin to say within yourselves—It must needs be that this is a good seed, or that the word is good, for it beginneth to enlarge my soul; yea, it beginneth to enlighten my understanding, yea, it beginneth to be delicious to me.
We do not need all the answers first. We only need to give the word room to grow. Then we can see what it does in us.

Those people never had the book—it was meant for us. Mormon, the ancient prophet after whom the book is named, abridged centuries of records. God, who knows the end from the beginning, told him what to include in his abridgment that we would need for our day.
It was meant for the time we live in.
A voice that steadies.
Helaman said to build on Christ, so storms cannot pull us down. Nephi said to press on with hope.

And now, my sons, remember, remember that it is upon the rock of our Redeemer, who is Christ, the Son of God, that ye must build your foundation; that when the devil shall send forth his mighty winds, yea, his shafts in the whirlwind, yea, when all his hail and his mighty storm shall beat upon you, it shall have no power over you to drag you down to the gulf of misery and endless wo, because of the rock upon which ye are built, which is a sure foundation, a foundation whereon if men build they cannot fall.

Wherefore, ye must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ, having a perfect brightness of hope, and a love of God and of all men. Wherefore, if ye shall press forward, feasting upon the word of Christ, and endure to the end, behold, thus saith the Father: Ye shall have eternal life.

God always provides safety for the soul, and with the Book of Mormon, He has again done that in our time.
When the world is loud, this voice stays calm.
Pass the voice on.
Lehi wanted his family to share in what he found. Alma hoped to bring souls to God.

And it came to pass that I did go forth and partake of the fruit thereof; and I beheld that it was most sweet, above all that I ever before tasted. Yea, and I beheld that the fruit thereof was white, to exceed all the whiteness that I had ever seen. And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit.

I know that which the Lord hath commanded me, and I glory in it. I do not glory of myself, but I glory in that which the Lord hath commanded me; yea, and this is my glory, that perhaps I may be an instrument in the hands of God to bring some soul to repentance; and this is my joy.

It contains the answers to life’s most compelling questions.
Someone near you may be waiting to hear it.

story.title: A small voice that pierced the soul

blocks.text: The people at the temple in Bountiful heard a voice from heaven.

And it came to pass that they heard a voice as if it came out of heaven; and they cast their eyes round about, for they understood not the voice which they heard; and it was not a harsh voice, neither was it a loud voice; nevertheless, and notwithstanding it being a small voice it did pierce them that did hear to the center, insomuch that there was no part of their frame that it did not cause to quake; yea, it did pierce them to the very soul, and did cause their hearts to burn.
At first they did not understand it. But they kept listening. When we read the Book of Mormon with a quiet heart, we can feel that same warmth.

story.title: Hear him

blocks.text: After the voice came the third time, the people understood it.
Behold my Beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, in whom I have glorified my name—hear ye him.
The Father pointed them to Jesus Christ. That is what the Book of Mormon does too. It points us to the Savior and invites us to build on Him.

application.text: First, read the Book of Mormon each day, even a little. Second, look for what it teaches about Jesus Christ. Third, make one change in your week to build on Him.
